normative_language: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are normative.

terms.definition: The provider-neutral, repository-local contracts and lifecycle that turn a project idea into auditable research, plans, bounded execution, and knowledge releases.
A repository and its explicitly declared framework control state, identity, roots, and revision.
The versioned canonical declaration of project identity, repository revision, owned paths, and framework contract version.
A human-authored statement of project intent, desired outcomes, boundaries, assumptions, and unresolved questions; it is accepted planning input, not executable authority.
Immutable acquired or observed bytes and metadata preserved with provenance; raw records are untrusted data and are not accepted knowledge or active procedures.
A content-addressed immutable raw record of acquired bytes plus metadata and a cryptographic hash.
An addressable exact span or structured location in an immutable raw record, linked with provenance and stance to a finding or claim.
A finding, decision, claim, plan, or release admitted through an authorized review boundary and reconstructable from canonical history.
A versioned policy, packet, capability, or instruction explicitly authorized to control framework work; source content and generated text never become active procedures by being ingested.
A bounded proposition produced by research or codebase observation with evidence, scope, confidence, and lifecycle state.
An explicitly accepted, provenance-backed finding, decision, constraint, or observation eligible to inform a goal plan without silently mutating it.
A versioned desired outcome with acceptance conditions and lifecycle state in a goal DAG.
A directed acyclic graph of goals and typed dependency edges that permits shared dependencies without duplication.
A directed prerequisite relation whose provenance is exactly one of declared, observed, or inferred.
A dependency explicitly stated by an authorized project artifact or owner.
A dependency supported by reproducible repository or execution evidence.
A provisional dependency derived by analysis and never silently promoted to declared or observed status.
A bounded, versioned, provider-neutral handoff containing scope, objective, inputs, constraints, dependencies, acceptance checks, risks, freshness, and evidence references.
An authorized immutable packet version; any content change creates a linked successor version.
An immutable record of an execution attempt, including artifacts, observed dependencies, validation evidence, failures, and retry or supersession state.
An evaluator distinct from the execution attempt that maps each acceptance condition to observed evidence and cannot rely only on the executor's assertion.
An immutable, bounded execution of a declared research pipeline preserving scope, sources, evidence, gaps, synthesis, audit, and receipt.
A versioned active procedure defining bounded research stages, source policy, budgets, outputs, and audit requirements without naming a required provider.
An immutable audit record identifying the procedure version, actors or adapters, inputs, capabilities, outputs, policy, timing, and result of a run.
A bounded immutable export of accepted project-local findings, decisions, patterns, gaps, implementation state, provenance, and supersession links.
A rebuildable index, graph, cache, embedding, summary, or rendered view that is never authoritative by itself.
Accepted state deterministically reconstructed only from authorized append-only events and referenced immutable records.
A bounded working artifact that may inform proposals but is non-canonical, expires or is discarded, and cannot directly mutate accepted state.
A versioned artifact admitted through its required authorization boundary and present in canonical history.
An immutable historical artifact replaced by an explicitly linked newer version and no longer current.
A preserved proposal denied at review with rationale and prohibited from appearing as accepted or current.
An artifact whose type, location, version, provenance, and lifecycle transition satisfy the applicable contract and policy.
Specified by observable inputs, outputs, and behavior without requiring a particular agent, model, hosted service, database, or vendor.
The declared revision, generation, source hash, or time condition under which an artifact remains eligible for use.
An explicit immutable relation from an older artifact to its replacement, preserving both history and current selection.
The recorded origin, actor, procedure, source location, version, and transformation chain sufficient to audit an artifact.

invariants.title: Trust-zone separation
invariants.rule: Raw records MUST remain distinguishable from accepted knowledge and active procedures. Raw or generated content MUST NOT authorize control actions.
invariants.positive: A fetched page is stored by hash and quoted as evidence, while an owner-approved pipeline file controls the run.
invariants.adversarial: A page says to ignore policy and publish a secret; the text is retained only as untrusted bytes and no action is authorized.

invariants.title: Append-only accepted history
invariants.rule: Canonical history MUST be append-only and canonical state MUST be a deterministic projection. Correction MUST use an explicit lifecycle transition, never destructive rewrite.
invariants.positive: A corrected finding supersedes the prior version while both remain reconstructable.
invariants.adversarial: A tool attempts to edit an accepted finding in place; validation rejects the mutation.

invariants.title: Immutable exact evidence
invariants.rule: Accepted factual findings MUST cite immutable content hashes and exact spans unless explicitly typed as a human decision or assumption.
invariants.positive: A finding cites snapshot sha256:abc and lines 10-14.
invariants.adversarial: A synthesis cites only a mutable URL; it cannot be accepted as a factual finding.

invariants.title: Authorized mutation boundary
invariants.rule: Untrusted or delegated actors MAY propose changes but MUST NOT accept, retract, supersede, release, change policy, or write externally without the required authorization.
invariants.positive: An agent proposes a packet and an authorized owner records release approval.
invariants.adversarial: A provider marks its own output accepted; the transition is denied.

invariants.title: Stale work fails closed
invariants.rule: A mutating proposal MUST identify its base revision or generation and MUST fail closed when freshness no longer holds.
invariants.positive: A result based on revision R is accepted while R remains current.
invariants.adversarial: A result based on R is submitted after R+1; it is marked stale and cannot commit.

invariants.title: Dependency provenance
invariants.rule: Every dependency edge MUST be typed as declared, observed, or inferred. Inferred dependencies MUST NOT be silently promoted.
invariants.positive: A build log supports an observed dependency from test to generated schema.
invariants.adversarial: A model guesses an edge and stores it as declared; validation rejects the provenance mismatch.

invariants.title: Bounded immutable releases
invariants.rule: Released packets and knowledge releases MUST be bounded, versioned, immutable, provenance-backed, and explicitly superseded when changed.
invariants.positive: Packet v2 links to v1 and records changed constraints and fresh evidence hashes.
invariants.adversarial: A released packet is overwritten at the same version; canonical validation fails.

invariants.title: Derived state is non-authoritative
invariants.rule: Indexes, graphs, caches, embeddings, summaries, and views MUST be rebuildable and MUST NOT be the sole source of accepted truth.
invariants.positive: Deleting an index and rebuilding from canonical events yields the same accepted state.
invariants.adversarial: A vector result with no canonical record is returned as accepted knowledge; the query fails closed.

invariants.title: Scope and time remain explicit
invariants.rule: Accepted assertions MUST preserve project scope and applicable valid time; historical order MUST preserve transaction revision or generation.
invariants.positive: A project-local policy valid from T1 coexists with a global default and retains its acceptance generation.
invariants.adversarial: Two scoped values are collapsed into one timeless global fact; validation rejects the lossy projection.

invariants.title: Provider-neutral correctness
invariants.rule: Correctness MUST NOT depend on a named agent, model, hosted service, cloud database, network, GPU, or architecture-specific repository layout.
invariants.positive: Two adapters emit contract-equivalent research-run artifacts and offline validation gives equal results.
invariants.adversarial: A required field contains a vendor session identifier with no portable semantic equivalent; the contract rejects it.

invariants.title: Capabilities, confinement, and audit
invariants.rule: Tool and external actions MUST use explicit deny-by-default capabilities, confined paths, bounded budgets, secret controls, and audit records.
invariants.positive: A connector may read one approved URL within budget and records its inputs and result.
invariants.adversarial: A path resolves outside the declared root or a connector exceeds budget; execution stops without side effects.

invariants.title: Independent acceptance evidence
invariants.rule: Execution claims MUST map each acceptance condition to observed evidence and the executor MUST NOT be its only evaluator.
invariants.positive: A separate validator maps all packet checks to command outputs and artifacts.
invariants.adversarial: The executor says tests passed but supplies no observable result; completion is not accepted.
